name: Arkansas
tagline: Ozark hollows, Ouachita ridges and Delta cotton fields, from Mount Magazine to Crowley's Ridge.
intro: Arkansas's byways climb into the Ozark and Ouachita national forests, follow Crowley's Ridge and the Great River Road across the Delta, and trace an 1864 Civil War march through the southwest pine country. This chapter follows the Arkansas Scenic Byways Program run by the Arkansas Department of Transportation, whose list mixes state, national and Forest Service designations and includes, unusually, a stretch of Interstate 530 and the I-49 leg of the Boston Mountains loop. Separately, the General Assembly has named some fifty state scenic highways by act since 1975, mostly unnamed segments, which are not covered here.

members.name: Camden Expedition Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A long loop out of Little Rock that traces General Steele's failed Union march of 1864, through Arkadelphia to the old Confederate capital at Washington, then east to Camden and back by way of Fordyce, Leola and Sheridan.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Crowley's Ridge Parkway National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A wooded ridge standing up to 200 feet above the flat Delta, followed north from the river town of Helena on a narrow forest road past Storm Creek Lake, then on through farm towns toward the Missouri line.

members.name: Arkansas Scenic 7 Byway
members.blurb: Highway 7 runs nearly the length of the state, from El Dorado through Camden and the bathhouses of Hot Springs, over the Ouachitas and the Arkansas River, and up through the Ozarks to the courthouse square in Harrison.

members.name: Boston Mountains Scenic Loop
members.blurb: Two roads over the Boston Mountains between Alma and Fayetteville: old US 71, winding through small mountain towns along the stagecoach country of the Butterfield mail, and the interstate, which bores through the state's only highway tunnel.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Great River Road National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Arkansas leg crosses flat Delta rice and cotton country, climbing Crowley's Ridge in the St. Francis forest, passing blues history at Helena and the Cash boyhood home at Dyess, and ending at oxbow Lake Chicot.

members.name: Highway 21/Ozark Highlands Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 21 leaves Clarksville for the Ozark National Forest and follows the ridges between creek headwaters, crossing the Ozark Highlands Trail on its way north to the Buffalo National River near Boxley.

members.name: Interstate 530
members.blurb: Fifteen miles of four-lane interstate swinging around the southwest side of Pine Bluff from White Hall, across Bayou Bartholomew and the flat alluvial plain; an unlikely byway, and one of the state's shortest.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Mount Magazine Scenic Byway/Highway 309
members.blurb: Highway 309 climbs from Havana onto Mount Magazine, the highest ground in Arkansas, with an overlook toward Blue Mountain Lake, then drops some 2,300 feet past Cove Lake to the courthouse town of Paris.

members.name: Pig Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 23 twists north from Ozark through the national forest on hairpin curves under a canopy of trees, crossing the Mulberry River and passing a roadside waterfall; generations of Razorback fans have driven it to Fayetteville.

members.name: Sylamore Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A short forest road that follows the White River through Optimus and Allison, then turns up into the hills to Blanchard Springs Caverns and the Mirror Lake historic district.

members.name: Talimena Scenic Drive National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 88 climbs out of Mena onto the crest of Rich Mountain, past Queen Wilhelmina State Park and through stunted ridge-top forest that was never logged, then follows the crest into Oklahoma.

members.name: West-Northwest Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A long backroad circuit of the western valleys: US 71 north from Mena through the Ouachita forest to Waldron and Greenwood, and Highway 10 east past Fort Chaffee, Booneville and Danville to Ola.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: St. Francis Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Twenty-one miles along the top of Crowley's Ridge between Marianna and Helena, much of it gravel, passing Bear Creek and Storm Creek lakes with glimpses down to the Mississippi and St. Francis bottoms.
